chunks: 4101 - He said: And I asked him about a man who pledged collateral with another man against one thousand dirhams, while the collateral was worth two thousand, and it was lost.

He said: "He returns against him for the surplus of what he pledged; and if it was less than that for which it was pledged, he returns against the pledger for the surplus; and if the collateral was equal to that for which it was pledged, then the collateral stands for what is in it."

key_terms.أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ: one thousand dirhams, the amount of the debt mentioned
key_terms.الرَّاهِنِ: the pledger, the one who gave the collateral
key_terms.الرَّهْنُ: the pledged property held as security
key_terms.بِفَضْلِ: for the surplus or excess amount
key_terms.رَهْنًا: collateral pledged as security for a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if pledged collateral is lost and its value is more, less, or equal to the debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a lost pledged asset in relation to the underlying debt. If the collateral exceeds the debt, its surplus is due back; if it falls short, the remaining amount is still owed by the pledger; and if equal, the collateral fully covers the debt.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4101 - He (narrator) said: I asked him about a man who deposited collateral (rahn) with another man against a debt of one thousand dirhams, while the value of the collateral was two thousand dirhams, but the collateral was lost.

Imam (as) said: "The creditor shall reclaim from the debtor the surplus value of what was pledged. If the value of the collateral was less than the debt, the creditor shall reclaim the remaining balance from the debtor. However, if the value of the collateral equaled the debt, then the collateral suffices as payment for the debt."
